connector: This is the last day with Harriet. You read a whole biography and three real accounts of one night. When accounts disagree, a good reader picks one to lean on and can say why. Which account would you trust, and what can none of them tell you?

notes.wordParts: Prefixes that tell where: trans- = across, inter- = between, sub- = under, super- = above or beyond: transportation, international, submarine, supernatural.
notes.grammar: Commas in a series: put a comma after each item in a list of three or more, including before and. She packed bread, cheese, and a knife. Editing day: check every list for its commas.
notes.spelling: Some words sound alike but mean different things. Affect is the action, effect is the result. It’s means it is; its shows belonging. Their means belonging to them, there is a place, they’re means they are. Accept means take; except means leave out.

read.label: Marcus · before you read the sources

transcripts.welcome: Hey, it’s Marcus. This is our last day with Harriet. You’ve read her whole life and three real accounts of her biggest night. Today’s question: what have you learned about how different writers tell the same story, and why it matters?
transcripts.read: Today you choose. If you had to tell a friend what happened on the Combahee, which account would you lean on? Say why: who wrote it, when, and how close they were. Then name one thing about that night none of them can tell you. Harriet could not write, but she still got her words printed.
transcripts.grammar: Editing day. Read every list in your writing out loud. If you hear three things, you need two commas. A comma can change what a sentence means, so don’t guess. Ask how many things are in the list, then count your commas. One more slow read, and you’re ready to present.

virtue.title: The freedom meter
virtue.moment: In 1863 one newspaper told the story of the raid without Harriet’s name. Weeks later, her own words were printed. Six years later, a whole book told her life. Almost a hundred years later, Dorothy Sterling wrote Freedom Train for young readers like you.
virtue.ask: How much does it matter who gets to tell the story? Slide to show.
virtue.take: One way to see it: Harriet could not read or write, so she dictated her letter. Without that, we would know the raid only as the work of “a black woman.”
virtue.name: freedom
